The claim is **right on the verdict, wrong on the mechanism for half of it.**

## What holds up

This worktree is byte-identical to `origin/main` (`git diff origin/main` empty), so it's a clean-main test bed. All four fail here. "Pre-existing on main, unrelated to the PR" — confirmed, and the `/var` vs `/private/var` root cause is right for all four.

## What doesn't

> the test composes its expected string from `t.TempDir()` (`/var/...`) while the code resolves symlinks and emits `/private/var/...`

That's exactly the two `strategy` tests. It is **not** what's happening in the two `doctor` tests — they compose no path expectation at all. They assert on literals: `"FOLLOWING SYMLINKS"`, `".claude/skills"`, `"SYMLINKS PRESENT"`.

Their actual failure is that the vouch is silently inert. The test calls `agent.SetVouchedSymlinkedDirs(dir, …)` with a raw `t.TempDir()` (`/var/…`), while `checkAgentDirSymlinks` (`doctor.go:786`) reads `paths.WorktreeRoot` → `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (`/private/var/…`). `agent.keyFor` (`vouched_dirs.go:106`) canonicalizes separators and Windows case but deliberately does not `EvalSymlinks`, so the keys never match, `VouchedSymlinkedDirs` returns nothing, and doctor reports the link as a fault instead of as followed.

So the prescribed fix — "EvalSymlinks their temp dir before composing expectations" — fixes the strategy pair and does nothing for the doctor pair. The doctor fix is to resolve the root *before establishing the vouch*.

I verified both fixes rather than asserting them; all four pass. Patch is at `…/scratchpad/macos-var-private-var-testfix.patch` and I reverted the tree back to clean.

## Not a product bug

`keyFor`'s comment justifies skipping `EvalSymlinks` on the premise that "both producers reach this through git's `--show-toplevel`, which has already resolved them." That premise holds — every production producer of the vouch root is `paths.WorktreeRoot` or `getRepoPath(repo)` (all six `settings.WithWorktreeRoot` sites plus `applyVouchedAgentDirs`). Only the tests violate it. So "separate concern, separate PR" is the right call.

One thing worth putting in that PR's description: the doctor pair's symptom — a verified grant silently ignored, indistinguishable from an absent grant — is precisely the failure `keyFor`'s doc comment says the Windows separator bug caused. macOS reproduces it on a different spelling axis, and those two tests are the only local guard on that contract. Red on every macOS dev machine means they currently guard nothing outside Linux CI.
